bind_list.description: List of IP addresses and ports for Hitch to listen on. Each entry may specify a custom address or port.

backend_list.description: List of backend application servers (HTTP/HTTPS) to proxy requests to.

default_cert.description: Path to default PEM file (certificate + private key) for TLS termination.

tls_versions.description: List of supported TLS protocol versions (order matters: most preferred first).

tls_prefer_server_ciphers.description: Whether to prefer server cipher ordering over client preference.

tls_cipher_suite.description: Optional explicit cipher suite string (e.g., 'ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:...'). If empty, defaults to Hitch's built-in secure suite.

ocsp_dir.description: Path to directory containing OCSP responder certificates for stapling. Leave empty to disable.

workers.description: Number of worker processes to spawn.

run_as_user.description: User account to run Hitch processes under (for security).

run_as_group.description: Group to run Hitch processes under.

pidfile_path.description: Path to PID file for process management.

keepalive_timeout.description: Seconds to keep idle connections alive on the frontend.

ssl_session_cache_enabled.description: Enable SSL session caching for faster reconnects.

ssl_session_cache_size.description: Maximum number of sessions to cache.

health_check_enabled.description: Enable passive backend health checks based on failed connections.

health_check_timeout.description: Seconds to wait before marking a backend as unhealthy.

health_check_expected_status.description: List of HTTP status codes considered healthy (e.g., [200, 204, 301]). Only used if health-check is enabled and backends respond via HTTP.

rate_limit_enabled.description: Enable connection rate limiting to mitigate abuse.

rate_limit_connections_per_second.description: Max new connections per second per frontend.

rate_limit_burst.description: Max concurrent connections allowed during burst periods.

http2_enabled.description: Enable HTTP/2 protocol on frontend connections.

http2_max_concurrent_streams.description: Maximum HTTP/2 concurrent streams per connection (0 = default).
